title: Containers: Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps

questions.sub_skill: Create and manage an Azure Container Registry
questions.prompt: Your registry must serve images from three regions under one name, and be reachable only through private endpoints. Which tier do you need?
options: Basic
Standard
Premium
Any tier, with geo-replication enabled per region
questions.explanation: Geo-replication and private link with private endpoints are Premium features.
why_not: Basic lacks geo-replication and private endpoints.
Standard adds capacity, not geo-replication or private endpoints.
Geo-replication requires the Premium tier.

questions.sub_skill: Create and manage an Azure Container Registry
questions.prompt: A container app's managed identity only needs to download images from your registry. Which role follows least privilege?
options: AcrPull
AcrPush
Owner
Contributor
questions.explanation: AcrPull grants data-plane read access to pull images and artifacts, with no write or control-plane permissions.
why_not: AcrPush also allows pushing images.
Owner is a privileged control-plane role, far beyond pulling.
Contributor manages the registry; it isn't the data-plane pull role.

questions.sub_skill: Create and manage an Azure Container Registry
questions.prompt: You must copy an image from Microsoft Container Registry into your Azure container registry from a workstation without Docker installed. What should you use?
options: docker pull then docker push
az acr build
Azure Storage Explorer
az acr import
questions.explanation: az acr import copies images from other registries directly into your registry without a local Docker installation.
why_not: That needs Docker.
acr build builds from source and a Dockerfile; it doesn't copy an existing image.
Storage Explorer manages storage accounts, not registries.

questions.sub_skill: Provision a container by using Azure Container Instances
questions.prompt: A data job runs in Azure Container Instances. If it fails it should be retried automatically, but once it completes successfully it must not run again. Which restart policy should you set?
options: Always
OnFailure
Never
Manual
questions.explanation: OnFailure restarts containers only when they fail, so a successful run ends the group in the Succeeded state while failures are retried.
why_not: Always restarts the container even after it completes successfully; it's the default and suits long-running services.
Never doesn't retry a failed run, which the requirement asks for.
There's no Manual restart policy; the options are Always, OnFailure and Never.

questions.sub_skill: Provision a container by using Azure Container Instances
questions.prompt: Two containers must share localhost networking, a lifecycle and a mounted volume in Azure Container Instances. How do you deploy them?
options: As two separate container groups on the same virtual network
As one Windows container group
As one Linux container group, defined in YAML or a template
As a container app with two revisions
questions.explanation: Containers in a container group share a host, lifecycle, local network and volumes. Multi-container groups are Linux only.
why_not: Separate groups don't share localhost or a lifecycle.
Multi-container groups are supported only for Linux.
Revisions are versions of one app, not co-located containers.

questions.sub_skill: Provision a container by using Azure Container Instances
questions.prompt: A container group must pull a private image from Azure Container Registry using a managed identity. The deployment fails because the identity isn't valid for the pull. What should you use?
options: A user-assigned managed identity with AcrPull, assigned to the group and named with --acr-identity
The container group's system-assigned identity
The registry's admin user
A Storage Blob Data Reader role on the registry
questions.explanation: ACI supports only a user-assigned managed identity for pulling from ACR, specified in both the group identity and imageRegistryCredentials.
why_not: For ACR image pulls, ACI supports only a user-assigned identity.
That works but isn't a managed identity, and Microsoft advises against it.
Registry pulls need AcrPull, not a storage role.

questions.sub_skill: Provision a container by using Azure Container Apps
questions.prompt: A web API must scale on concurrent HTTP requests and cost nothing for compute when idle overnight. Which service and settings fit?
options: Azure Container Instances with restart policy OnFailure
Azure Container Apps with a CPU scale rule and minimum replicas 0
Azure Container Registry Premium
Azure Container Apps with minimum replicas 0 and an HTTP scale rule
questions.explanation: Container Apps scales to zero with HTTP, TCP or event rules, and incurs no usage charges at zero replicas.
why_not: ACI has no rule-based scaling and doesn't scale to zero on traffic.
CPU and memory scale rules can't scale to zero.
A registry stores images; it doesn't run them.

questions.sub_skill: Provision a container by using Azure Container Apps
questions.prompt: You must route 10% of users to a new version of a container app while 90% stay on the current one. What do you configure?
options: Single revision mode with two containers
Multiple revision mode, and traffic weights of 90 and 10 on the two revisions
Two container apps behind separate URLs
A second Container Apps environment
questions.explanation: Multiple revision mode keeps several revisions active, and traffic splitting assigns percentage weights that must total 100.
why_not: Single mode routes all traffic to the latest ready revision.
That isn't a traffic split on one app's URL.
Environments don't split an app's traffic.

questions.sub_skill: Provision a container by using Azure Container Apps
questions.prompt: A container app was created with a public image. It must now pull a private image from ACR using its system-assigned identity. What is needed?
options: Enable the registry's admin user
Create a user-assigned identity; system-assigned isn't supported
Set the app's registry to use the system identity, ensure the identity has AcrPull, then update the image
Recreate the app in multiple revision mode
questions.explanation: Container Apps can use a system-assigned identity for ACR pulls (az containerapp registry set --identity system); the identity needs AcrPull.
why_not: Managed identity avoids shared admin credentials.
That restriction applies to ACI, not Container Apps.
Revision mode doesn't affect registry authentication.

questions.sub_skill: Manage sizing and scaling for containers, including Azure Container Instances and Azure Container Apps
questions.prompt: A container group runs with 1 CPU and 1.5 GB memory and now needs 2 CPUs. What must you do?
options: Delete the container group and re-create it with the new CPU value
Update the group in place with the new CPU value
Add an autoscale rule on CPU
Restart the group with a higher limit
questions.explanation: Changes to CPU, memory or GPU, restart policy, OS type, network profile or zone require deleting the container group first.
why_not: CPU, memory and GPU changes require deleting and redeploying the group.
Container Instances has no autoscale rules.
A restart doesn't change requested resources.

questions.sub_skill: Manage sizing and scaling for containers, including Azure Container Instances and Azure Container Apps
questions.prompt: A container app has min 0, max 10 replicas, and an HTTP rule of 10 concurrent requests per replica. 45 concurrent requests arrive. Roughly how many replicas run?
options: 1, because the minimum is 0
10, because the maximum is always used
45, one per request
About 5, within the maximum of 10
questions.explanation: The HTTP rule adds replicas when concurrent requests exceed the threshold, up to the maximum: 45 requests at 10 per replica needs about 5.
why_not: The rule adds replicas as concurrency exceeds 10 per replica.
Replicas follow demand up to the maximum, not straight to it.
Each replica handles up to the configured concurrency.

questions.sub_skill: Manage sizing and scaling for containers, including Azure Container Instances and Azure Container Apps
questions.prompt: An administrator adds a second scale rule to a container app using the Azure CLI, and the first rule disappears. Why?
options: Container Apps supports only one scale rule
Adding a scale rule with the CLI to an app that already has one replaces the existing rule
The first rule expired after 24 hours
Single revision mode allows only one rule
questions.explanation: Microsoft notes that adding a scale rule via the CLI replaces the existing one. Define multiple rules together.
why_not: Multiple rules are supported; defined together, any of them can trigger scaling.
Scale rules don't expire.
Revision mode doesn't limit the number of rules.
